findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and state whether the completion-verifier reviewer prompt (completion_verifier.md:80-98) and the CompletionVerdict `kind` contract enum (contracts.py:116) must also name `[non-codebase]`, or explicitly justify excluding them because the tag regex already accepts both spellings and the prompt token is only a classifier label.
evidence: completion_verifier.md:93-95: 'How you classify a criterion: SOLELY from an author tag ... Matching is exact and case-insensitive on the token `operator-attested`.'
completion_verifier.md:80 heading 'Criterion kinds: codebase-verifiable vs operator-attested' and :88 the kind label 'operator-attested'
contracts.py:116 kind Field description: 'codebase-verifiable | operator-attested (the criterion's evidence kind).'
The plan's 'What' lists only txn.py and completion_reconcile.py; the verifier prompt and contract enum are not enumerated.
Contrast: det_operator_attested.py:49 regex accepts BOTH spellings, so the DET guards tolerate the rename — but the LLM prompt/contract do not.
findings.finding: The LLM classification surface that keys on the tag value vocabulary is out of scope: the completion-verifier reviewer prompt and the structured-output contract still name `operator-attested`, so after the remediation strings are cut to `[non-codebase]` the model is told to accept a different token than the remediation instructs the author to write.
findings.location: What section (file list: txn.py + completion_reconcile.py only); AC line 3 (end-to-end re-verify)
scenarios: An author reads the new [non-codebase] remediation, tags their AC [non-codebase], and re-verifies; the verifier prompt still says the classification token is `operator-attested`, risking the criterion being classified codebase-verifiable and re-failing.
The model emits `kind: operator-attested` per the contract enum while user-facing text now says [non-codebase], producing inconsistent verdict vocabulary.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add completion_verifier.md and contracts.py:116 to the cutover scope (so the classification token/kind vocabulary the LLM keys on matches the remediation the author is told to follow), or add a Note to the plan explaining that the model-facing classification token stays `operator-attested` by design because _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE accepts both, and confirm AC-3's re-verify path exercises a `[non-codebase]`-tagged criterion end-to-end.
